subtopics.title: Base Times Height — the Single Volume Law

questions.question: The volume of every right prism and cylinder equals:
options: Perimeter of the base times height
Area of the base times the perpendicular height
Sum of all the face areas
Base times height divided by two

questions.question: A closed tea box measures 9 cm by 4 cm by 10 cm. Its volume is:

In the volume law, the 'height' is always:
options: The longest edge of the solid
The vertical edge, whatever the orientation
The perpendicular distance between the two identical faces
The slant length of the solid

A rectangle with sides h and πr²

subtopics.title: Working a Triangular Prism End to End

questions.question: A right-angled triangular base has legs 5 cm and 12 cm. Its area is:

The shortcut for the three rectangular faces of a triangular prism is:
options: Perimeter of the triangle times the prism's length

questions.question: Why may the hypotenuse NOT serve as the triangle's height in the area formula?
options: It is too long to be a height
Perpendicular height must pair with the base it is perpendicular to — the legs form that pair
The hypotenuse is never given in questions
It may — the answer is the same
